Figure 1:Declarative Attention (DA) lets a model control its own attention span.(Prompt)A system instruction, long context information divided into segments that we refer to as “magic chunks”, the user’s question, and the DA instruction.(Model Response)The model freely alternates between three modes:<global>navigates the full context,<focus>reasons upon the named chunk, and<local>reasons upon the information accumulated in the response so far.
Our protocol does not restrict how, when, or how many times each mode is used.(Declarative Attention Mask)A segment-level attention mask is derived from the model response text based on the DA syntax.
Each row represents the global, focus, and local reasoning steps, respectively.
The scaffold (system, question, instruction) stays attended in every mode, whilecontext segmentsare masked (dashed) except those the mode keeps: all segments under<global>, the focused segment (marked F) under<focus>, and none under<local>.
DA needs no auxiliary scorer and runs on off-the-shelf models with no training.
